back: adverb
returning to a place, person or earlier state
typical: come/go/get/give/call back, be back. NOT for: the rear part.
I'll be back at five.
She gave the book back.
noun
the part of your body behind your chest
typical: back pain, on your back. NOT for: the rear of an object.
My back hurts.
He lay on his back.
noun
the rear part of something
typical: the back of + noun, at the back. NOT for: body parts.
Sit at the back of the room.
Write your name on the back of the page.
adjective
at or near the rear
typical: back door/seat/garden. NOT for: returning.
She sat in the back seat.
We left by the back door.
verb
support someone or something
typical: back a plan/team/idea. NOT for: moving a vehicle.
The government backed the plan.
Many people backed the new law.
verb
move backwards, especially a vehicle
typical: back the car, back into/out of. NOT for: support.
He backed the car out of the garage.
The truck backed into the street.
